rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this iteration escalates obfuscation intensity: SecurityGain and DiversityGain weights are raised across all passes (especially SUB, FLA, and BCF) to push the selector toward applying transforms wherever features permit, while RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are lowered because the program is tiny (4 functions, ~1.1 KB text) and dominated by a bit-reversal loop with ample headroom for overhead. SPLIT and IGV are boosted as low-risk diversity multipliers that flatten structure and obscure variable provenance cheaply; ICALL stays moderately weighted since indirect dispatch hides call graphs in this small binary without excessive indirect-call overhead; CorrectnessRisk weights remain at moderate levels (0.3-0.6) so risk-aware functions like ReverseBits32/ReverseBits64 still gate the riskier control-flow transforms, preserving the verified correctness from round 1.
